steps.title: The choice is about status, not about time
steps.html:
All the forms below refer to time after now, and none of them is a future tense. What you are choosing between is how settled the event is and where the decision came from.

Will is the neutral one. Use it for a prediction or an opinion about later, and for a decision you are taking as you speak: I think I will apply. It carries no evidence with it, which is why it is so often paired with probably, I expect, I think. Be going to does two jobs: it reports an intention you formed before this conversation (I am going to work in my parents’ shop), and it predicts from evidence you can point at now (unemployment is high, so it is going to be hard). The present continuous is for arrangements — the date is agreed, the place is booked, another person or an institution is involved. The present simple is for timetables: departures, terms, kick-off times, opening hours. It is the form you use when the schedule is not yours to change.

steps.title: Degrees of certainty
steps.html:
• certain: will definitely, is definitely going to, starts at nine
  • probable: will probably, is likely to, I expect, I doubt (for the negative)
  • possible: might, may, could, there is a chance that
  • Negatives behave differently: probably goes before won’t but after will — She will probably come / She probably won’t come.

steps.title: Напиши свой текст
steps.sub: Напиши ответ, затем сверься с образцом
steps.modelHtml:
Ten years from now, almost nobody in my field will be paid for translating a menu or a contract. You can see it already: two of the four agencies in my city closed last year, and the work that is left is checking what a machine has produced. It is going to be a difficult decade for anybody who does only that.

So I am investing in the part a machine still cannot do. I am taking a course in conference interpreting in February — it starts on the eighth and runs for eleven months — and I have already turned down two invitations to work that would have made it impossible. When I finish, I intend to look for work with courts and hospitals rather than with agencies, because those rooms need a person in them.

I might also move to another country for a year, although that is likely to depend on the exchange rate rather than on me. What would prove me wrong is simple enough: if the machines learn to hear as well as they read, the whole plan needs a few large adjustments.
